To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in a large empty environment, mice perform knot-scribblings in a circumscribed locale that they establish in it.
mice establish a place in an open field environment that is characterized by high path tortuosity.
the behavior of mice exploring an open field is characterized by the performance of a long-lasting, centrally located, self-generated, and highly tortuous path, termed knot-scribblin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of a new type of marked place in mouse open field exploration, the knot.
the establishment of a novel place in the environment and the behavior that is performed in it.
the establishment of a novel form of behavior, knot-scribblings, and its role in exploration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

knots represent a novel and distinct form of exploration in which the mouse is engaged in an active search of a particular place, in which it then performs a highly tortuous behavior, and which is maintained both within a session and across sessions.
knots are a type of attractive place in the mouse open field.
knot-scribblers are “exploring the world in a different way” than non-scribblers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knots represent attractive places in the mouse open field.
mice mark places in an environment by knot-scribblings, and that these places are associated with high arousal.
mice mark places by scribbling, a behavior that involves the generation of multiple views and rich vestibular input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mice mark attractive places by performing a particular type of behavior, and that the behavior itself can be a source for self-generated landmarks.
mice can establish and maintain long-lasting associations between particular places and particular behaviors.
mice can use their locomotor behavior to mark a locale and that this marking is associated with a high level of arousal.
